newsitem.title: USA: Intensiva says on track for profit in '97.
newsitem.headline: Intensiva says on track for profit in '97.

text.p: Intensiva HealthCare Corp said on Tuesday it is on track to reach its goal of achieving profitability on a corporate-wide basis in 1997.

Earlier, it reported third quarter net loss of $1,596,743, compared with a year-ago loss of $772,940. For the first nine months, it had a net loss of $3,346,714, compared with a year-ago loss of $1,973,776.
"Our growth plan calls for opening 11 facilities in 1997," David Cross, president, said in a statement.
Intensiva, which completed a public offering on October 10, had seven facilities in operation at the end of the third quarter and will open three in the fourth quarter.
Future expansion will be financed with proceeds of its public offering. It received nearly $14 million from the offering and another $2.1 million from the over-allotment.

Intensiva, which provides highly specialized, acute long-term care for critically ill or injured patients, said its facilities typically incur losses during the first six to seven months of operation.
